answer: An identity registration locks a bond of 600 copper-denominated tokens for 20 epochs and must present one hardware credential per device serial, verified once by the registry. Forging N identities locks 600N tokens, each slashed 90 percent on proof of duplicate credential, and the remainder pent for 20 epochs. Splitting a stake across many keys multiplies the locked river of capital per identity while a shared slashing penalty raises the marginal cost above any ocean of accreted rewards.
